article_title: Separating Myth from Reality in Education: Introduction to the Special Issue
citation: Andrew C. Butler & Shana K. Carpenter. (2015). Separating Myth from Reality in Education: Introduction to the Special Issue. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-015-9344-0
title: A four-step evaluative framework for judging educational practices and beliefs
description: The editorial describes a shared evaluation process modeled by every article in the special issue. Each article first documents that a practice or belief exists, then sets objective criteria for what would count as good experimental evidence, then weighs the evidence for and against, and finally draws conclusions and recommendations. The editors argue this process "provides a roadmap for evaluating other practices and beliefs in education as well as other fields."
requirements: Delineation of objective criteria for judging efficacy or accuracy before weighing evidence, since "Many of the disagreements about practices and beliefs stem from a lack of common understanding about criteria for evaluating claims."
target_learning_goals: identifying effective practices and accurate beliefs about learning
examples: Each special-issue article "begin[s] by defining and documenting the existence of the practice or belief," then evaluates evidence against criteria it sets up.
key_sources: Andrew C. Butler & Shana K. Carpenter. (2015). Separating Myth from Reality in Education: Introduction to the Special Issue. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-015-9344-0

article_title: Spaced Retrieval Practice Imposes Desirable Difficulty in Calculus Learning
citation: Keith B. Lyle, Campbell R. Bego, Patricia A. S. Ralston, Jason C. Immekus. (2022). Spaced Retrieval Practice Imposes Desirable Difficulty in Calculus Learning. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-022-09677-2
title: Spaced versus massed MyMathLab quizzing procedure with end-of-semester criterial test
description: A classroom research procedure embedded in a hybrid calculus course for engineering undergraduates using the MyMathLab online platform. For each of 24 target learning objectives, MyMathLab generated "three random algorithmic variants of the question for each student", which were presented either on a single quiz (massed) or distributed across three consecutive biweekly quizzes (spaced), with assignment of objective sets to condition counterbalanced across students. Retention was measured by a 24-question criterial test on the last day of class, proctored via ProctorU, with quizzes and the test averaged to count for 7% of the course grade.
requirements: A question library with algorithmic variants (drawn primarily from Thomas' Calculus)
Biweekly quizzes accessible within a timed window, completed in one sitting
Counterbalanced assignment of objective sets to massed versus spaced conditions
constraints: Quizzes were not proctored; the authors relied on time limits, randomized question order, and algorithmic variants to deter answer sharing
Attrition left slightly unbalanced counterbalancing groups (92 vs. 88 of N = 180)
target_learners: engineering undergraduates in a first-semester calculus course
target_learning_goals: retention of fundamental calculus objectives from the first seven weeks of the course
examples: Quizzes were administered at the end of weeks 3, 5, 7, 9, and 11, with approximately 3 minutes allowed per question
key_sources: Keith B. Lyle, Campbell R. Bego, Patricia A. S. Ralston, Jason C. Immekus. (2022). Spaced Retrieval Practice Imposes Desirable Difficulty in Calculus Learning. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-022-09677-2

article_title: Myartspace: Design and evaluation of support for learning with multimedia phones between classrooms and museums
citation: Vavoula, G., Sharples, M., Rudman, P., Meek, J., & Lonsdale, P. (2009). Myartspace: Design and evaluation of support for learning with multimedia phones between classrooms and museums. Computers & Education. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2009.02.007
title: Myartspace mobile service for inquiry-led learning across museum and classroom
description: Myartspace is a service using mobile phones and a website to support inquiry learning between classrooms and museums. Students collect photos, audio recordings, text comments, and objects via two-letter exhibit codes during a museum visit; content is automatically sent by GPRS to personal online stores. In post-visit lessons students create personal galleries synthesising collected evidence to answer inquiry questions set in a pre-visit lesson.
requirements: Museums must digitise content for the museum store
Teachers receive a Teacher's Pack and Lesson Plans and customise the three-lesson sequence
constraints: Phones are locked to the Myartspace application and cannot be used for calls
Audio and text comments made when a photograph is taken are not linked to the photograph
target_learners: secondary school students (Key Stage 3, ages 13-14 in the trial)
target_learning_goals: inquiry-based collecting, selection and synthesis of museum evidence
examples: Students at the D-Day museum were set the question 'Was D-Day a triumph or disaster for Britain?'
key_sources: Vavoula, G., Sharples, M., Rudman, P., Meek, J., & Lonsdale, P. (2009). Myartspace: Design and evaluation of support for learning with multimedia phones between classrooms and museums. Computers & Education. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2009.02.007

article_title: Characterization of the learning environment for teaching pharmaceutical care: a scoping review.
citation: Ribeiro MAL, Hohenfeld DWA, Tavares TMA, Araújo-Neto FC, Mesquita AR, Brito GC, Lyra Jr DP. (2026). Characterization of the learning environment for teaching pharmaceutical care: a scoping review. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-08876-7
title: MyDispense virtual community pharmacy simulation
description: MyDispense is a virtual simulation tool used in one included study to teach dispensing skills. The review describes that "MyDispense simulated a community pharmacy offering representations of patients, prescriptions, products on shelves, and a high-fidelity interface to prescription processing". It is cited among tools that improved performance, confidence, and learning, complementing online activities with formative feedback, and was considered effective for developing dispensing abilities.
requirements: Integration with online activities and formative feedback
target_learners: Undergraduate pharmacy students (1st year in the reported study)
examples: The review's Table 5 records the virtual simulated activities study's main result: the tool was considered effective for developing dispensing abilities
key_sources: Ribeiro MAL, Hohenfeld DWA, Tavares TMA, Araújo-Neto FC, Mesquita AR, Brito GC, Lyra Jr DP. (2026). Characterization of the learning environment for teaching pharmaceutical care: a scoping review. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-08876-7

article_title: Benefits and Meanings of Educating with Videogames in a Puerto Rican Sixth Grade Public School Classroom
citation: Vélez-Agosto, N. M. & Rivas-Vélez, A. (2018). Benefits and meanings of educating with videogames in a Puerto Rican sixth grade public school classroom. International Journal of Educational Technology, 5(1), 9-19. http://educationaltechnology.net/ijet/
title: My English Coach (Spanish Edition) for Nintendo DS as a classroom English-learning game
description: My English Coach (Spanish Edition) is an educational game developed and published by Ubisoft, released in 2009 for the Nintendo DS. "The videogame teaches the basics of word use, grammar, and construction of phrases through mini -games, and evaluates your progress." It begins with a placement test, teaches pronunciation via voice recording and playback comparison to a native speaker, uses eight mini-games to reinforce lessons, and contains 10,000 English words plus a built-in Spanish-English dictionary and phrase book with 400 phrases. In the study it was played twenty minutes daily for four weeks by the experimental group.
requirements: A Nintendo DS console and teacher training on the game's use and instructions
constraints: The game software is not based on state or national sixth grade English school curriculum
target_learners: sixth-grade students learning English as a second language
target_learning_goals: English word use, grammar, phrase construction, and pronunciation
examples: The experimental group played the game twenty minutes every day of the week for four weeks, with weekly archived game-playing logs of time, scores, mastered words, and lesson levels
key_sources: Vélez-Agosto, N. M. & Rivas-Vélez, A. (2018). Benefits and meanings of educating with videogames in a Puerto Rican sixth grade public school classroom. International Journal of Educational Technology, 5(1), 9-19. http://educationaltechnology.net/ijet/

article_title: Effect of the Use of Multimedia on Students' Performance: A Case Study of Social Studies Class
citation: Genç Osman Ilhan and Şahin Oruç. (2016). Effect of the use of multimedia on students’ performance: A case study of social studies class. Educational Research and Reviews.
title: Multimedia material set for the 'My Friends Away' social studies unit
description: A set of multimedia sources assembled for the experimental group's 10-hour implementation of the 4th-grade unit 'My Friends Away'. It included power-point presentations, audio-music records, animations and videos, chosen, in the article's words, to "address the students‟ visual and audial senses". The 'finding countries' activity was studied on a computer platform and completed by students enjoyably as if playing a game, and student-level-compatible documentary cuts about the countries and cultures in the unit were watched.
requirements: Computer platform access for the finding-countries activity
Materials aligned with the Ministry of National Education's objectives for the unit
constraints: Power-point presentations and audio-music records were designed with researcher-experts, while animations and videos were taken as they were
target_learning_goals: Knowledge of countries, flags and cultures covered in the 'My Friends Away' unit
examples: Students completed the computer-based 'finding countries' activity with enjoyment as if they were playing a game; music and audio records about the Turkish countries were listened to and common points highlighted.
key_sources: Genç Osman Ilhan and Şahin Oruç. (2016). Effect of the use of multimedia on students’ performance: A case study of social studies class. Educational Research and Reviews. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1099996

article_title: Computer-Assisted Pronunciation Learning in a Collaborative Context: A Case Study in Taiwan
citation: Tsai Pi-hua. (2015). Computer-Assisted Pronunciation Learning in a Collaborative Context: A Case Study in Taiwan. TOJET: The Turkish Online Journal of Educational Technology, 14(4). https://www.tojet.net/
title: MyET computer-assisted pronunciation training software with visual pitch-contour feedback
description: MyET is a CAPT program designed in Taiwan by LLabs Inc. that "uses advanced audio and visual technology" to raise learners' awareness of their pronunciation problems. It provides automated speech recognition comparing a student's production with a native-speaker model, visual feedback such as contrasts between the learner's and a model teacher's pitch contours, and scores across pronunciation, intonation, timing, and intensity components. In this study it supplied the practice materials and feedback for two experimental groups over ten weeks.
requirements: Recorded learner speech input for the automated speech recognition to analyze
Model utterances against which learner production is compared
constraints: Participants reported fluctuating scores and feedback that did not always tell them how to modify production to match the model utterances
target_learning_goals: English pronunciation, intonation, timing, and intensity
examples: Participants practiced Part I of Cinderella and Part I of The Three Billy Goats in MyET, which displays loudness, timing, intonation, pronunciation, and total scores in its learning interface
key_sources: Tsai Pi-hua. (2015). Computer-Assisted Pronunciation Learning in a Collaborative Context: A Case Study in Taiwan. TOJET: The Turkish Online Journal of Educational Technology, 14(4). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1077659

article_title: The Effect of Active Learning Approach on Student Achievement in Secondary School 5th Grade English Course
citation: Yenen, E. T., & Dursun, F. (2019). The Effect of Active Learning Approach on Student Achievement in Secondary School 5th Grade English Course. Novitas-ROYAL (Research on Youth and Language), 13(2), 175-186. https://dergipark.org.tr/en/pub/novitas
title: Researcher-built 38-question 'My Town' achievement test with test-retest reliability of .83
description: The researchers built an achievement test aligned to the Ministry of National Education (MONE, 2016) fifth-grade English curriculum outcomes for the 'My Town' unit. "The achievement test consists of 38 questions prepared in differe nt question types." Content validity was checked by three English teachers, and reliability was estimated by test-retest: "The Pearson correlation coefficient between the two tests in the study was .83." It served as pre-test, post-test, and permanence test.
requirements: Administered to the same individuals twice for the test-retest reliability estimate, piloted with 25 fifth-grade students over a three-week period
constraints: Teachers interviewed suggested the test could be expanded with additional question types such as understanding and giving simple directions
target_learners: Fifth-grade secondary school students learning English as a foreign language
target_learning_goals: 'My Town' unit learning outcomes: describing places, giving directions, and related vocabulary
examples: Used as pre-test, post-test, and four-week delayed permanence test for both experimental and control groups
key_sources: Yenen, E. T., & Dursun, F. (2019). The Effect of Active Learning Approach on Student Achievement in Secondary School 5th Grade English Course. Novitas-ROYAL (Research on Youth and Language), 13(2), 175-186. https://dergipark.org.tr/en/pub/novitas

article_title: The Effect of Web Assisted Learning with Emotional Intelligence Content on Students' Information about Energy Saving, Attitudes towards Environment and Emotional Intelligence
citation: Ercan, O., Ural, E., & Köse, S. (2017). The Effect of Web Assisted Learning with Emotional Intelligence Content on Students' Information about Energy Saving, Attitudes Towards Environment and Emotional Intelligence. Science Education International, 28(1), 78-94. https://www.stes.org.tr
title: My environment and energy: web-assisted software enriched with emotional intelligence content
description: The educational software "My environment and energy" delivers environment and energy-saving content through sections including "What do I know?", "Clouds installed with emotions", "A Different World" and "Entertainment". It opens with prior-knowledge questions whose answers appear on a teacher panel so misconceptions can be determined. It "tried to develop the empathy skills of the students and their environmental awareness", linking environmental pollution to disease in the body and reminding students of the principle "don't do anything which you do not want done to yourself". It was encoded with Microsoft Visual Studio C# 2008, with visuals in Adobe Photoshop CS4 and animations in Adobe Flash CS4 Professional.
requirements: A teacher panel to display students' answers to the prior-knowledge questions during class
constraints: Content limited to environment and energy-saving topics as processed under the software's headings
examples: Used three weeks with the experimental group in place of traditional lecture on the same subject
key_sources: Ercan, O., Ural, E., & Köse, S. (2017). The Effect of Web Assisted Learning with Emotional Intelligence Content on Students' Information about Energy Saving, Attitudes Towards Environment and Emotional Intelligence. Science Education International, 28(1), 78-94. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1143753

article_title: Exploring the Skills Prioritised in the Assessment of Students Pursuing Adult Nursing, Post-COVID: A Qualitative Analysis.
citation: Bond, Carmel, Painter, Joanna M., Barnett, Donna. (2025). Exploring the Skills Prioritised in the Assessment of Students Pursuing Adult Nursing, Post‐COVID: A Qualitative Analysis. Nursing Open. https://doi.org/10.1002/nop2.70236
title: MYEPAD online practice assessment document for UK student nurses
description: MYEPAD (Midlands, Yorkshire and East Practice Assessment Document) is an online practice assessment document produced collaboratively between 28 universities, used in this study as the data source. The article states it "was developed to ensure that student nurses are prepared to successfully meet the Future Nurse: Standards of Proficiency for Registered Nurses" at registration, and it details the level of performance students must demonstrate at the end of each year of study. Sections are structured so practice assessors comment on students' 'knowledge, skills, attitudes and values'.
requirements: Completion by practice assessors working with practice supervisors and academic assessors as part of the collaborative 'triple assessment' model
constraints: Designed for UK pre-registration nursing programmes aligned to the NMC 2018 Future Nurse standards
target_learners: pre-registration student nurses in UK undergraduate nursing programmes
target_learning_goals: NMC Future Nurse standards of proficiency
examples: The study extracted 81 assessor comments from the MYEPAD documentation of second-year adult nursing students
key_sources: Bond, Carmel, Painter, Joanna M., Barnett, Donna. (2025). Exploring the Skills Prioritised in the Assessment of Students Pursuing Adult Nursing, Post‐COVID: A Qualitative Analysis. Nursing Open. https://doi.org/10.1002/nop2.70236

citation: Ritter Christoph. (2025). Digitale Lernmethoden in der Pharmazie [Digital learning methods in pharmacy]. Bundesgesundheitsblatt, Gesundheitsforschung, Gesundheitsschutz. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00103-025-04041-5
title: MyDispense Germany: game-like dispensing simulation software and the MyDispense Netzwerk Deutschland
description: MyDispense, a simulation software developed at Monash University, creates a virtual space in which medicines are dispensed, with dispensing situations in a community pharmacy, a hospital outpatient department, or a ward request. Since 2017 Universität Greifswald adapted it with the Australian developers to German conditions; "Seit 2019 steht so eine MyDispense-Version für Deutschland bereit." Exercises range from formal prescription checks to dispensing on prescription and self-medication, with automated feedback after each exercise and lecturer-assessed assessment exercises. Because interest existed at other sites, "wurde das MyDispense Netzwerk Deutschland gegründet".
requirements: Adaptation to national legal framework conditions (prescription form design and requirements), a nationally representative drug assortment, population of the software with various person types, and translation of all user-visible information into German
constraints: Each process step is completed with an assessment exercise graded by the lecturer; the article does not report comparative effectiveness data for the software in this text
target_learners: pharmacy students in clinical pharmacy courses at German-speaking universities
target_learning_goals: assessing dispensing situations, using professional literature, capturing patient data, gathering information in conversations with patients and physicians
examples: The network's core is an exchange platform for MyDispense exercises and associated learning materials, plus personal exchange among lecturers via online conference four times a year
key_sources: Ritter Christoph. (2025). Digitale Lernmethoden in der Pharmazie [Digital learning methods in pharmacy]. Bundesgesundheitsblatt, Gesundheitsforschung, Gesundheitsschutz. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00103-025-04041-5

article_title: The effectiveness of a structured validated questionnaire to assess student perception with virtual pharmacy simulation in pharmacy practice experiential education.
citation: Palanisamy A, Hameed PMSH, Prabhu VV, Mohideen NTM, Falah AM, Muralikrishnan D, Vasudevan M, Sayed AMA. (2024). The effectiveness of a structured validated questionnaire to assess student perception with virtual pharmacy simulation in pharmacy practice experiential education. PLoS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0314117
title: MyDispense virtual pharmacy simulation with communication and technical skill exercises integrated into IPPE2 and APPE courses
description: MyDispense is "a digital education platform that enables students to practice the skills of a pharmacist, from novice to highly advanced, in a safe virtual environment that is web-based and highly accessible". Exercises simulated virtual patients seeking prescriptions and covered patient fact-finding, patient education, answering patient questions, prescription monitoring, labeling, and dispensing. At the University of Tabuk it was integrated for four weeks of thirteen-week IPPE2 and APPE courses, with a demonstration, tutorial exercise, formative assessment and summative assessment in sequence.
requirements: Computer lab with internet facilities as the article states exercises were conducted in
Instructor demonstration of the MyDispense exercise and evaluation rubrics in the first week
constraints: Previous research reports barriers including lack of staff training in building cases, lack of realism, and challenges harmonizing drug nomenclature
Surveys were not permitted before or after the summative assessment by University policy
target_learning_goals: Communication skills such as patient fact-finding and patient education
examples: Exercises included prescription monitoring of items such as drug-drug interactions, and dispensing of the right patient, drug, dose, quantity and formulation
key_sources: Palanisamy A, Hameed PMSH, Prabhu VV, Mohideen NTM, Falah AM, Muralikrishnan D, Vasudevan M, Sayed AMA. (2024). The effectiveness of a structured validated questionnaire to assess student perception with virtual pharmacy simulation in pharmacy practice experiential education. PLoS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0314117
